issues.legal_issue: A choultry may include a unified complex of lodging and incidental facilities intended to serve pilgrims and travellers.
material_facts: The building provided lodging for pilgrims on its ground and first floors, including some rooms for which small service charges were collected.
Offices, shops, a canteen, transport facilities, a laundry, a barber shop, a post office and other facilities were located within the building or its campus and were intended to serve pilgrims.
The facilities and lodging operated as one institution, and the evidence showed no profit motive in providing the facilities.
issues.conclusion: The choultry could not be separated from the offices, shops and other facilities principally provided to serve its visitors; the complex was to be assessed as a whole by its predominant purpose.
issues.legal_principle: Section 83(1)(b) of the Madras District Municipalities Act, 1920 exempts qualifying choultries. Because the Act does not define “choultry,” the Court considered its ordinary and popular meaning as a shelter or resting place for travellers, and applied the predominant-intention test to a modern, self-contained complex. Facilities incidental or subservient to the choultry’s charitable lodging purpose may form part of it, but a separate property or profit-making enterprise does not thereby become a choultry. The Court distinguished Kesarapalli Anjaneyulu v. Eluru Municipality, Sri Kanyakaparameswari Anna Satram v. Vijayawada Municipality, Kodandaram Pillai v. Municipal Council, Trichinopoly, and Pandarasannadhi v. Corporation of Madras on their facts.

rule.if: tax_exemption_appeal and pilgrim_lodging_is_predominant and ancillary_facilities_serve_lodgers and not profit_motive

predicates.tax_exemption_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning whether property is exempt from municipal property tax as a choultry.
predicates.pilgrim_lodging_is_predominant: The property is principally organized and used to provide lodging or shelter to pilgrims or travellers.
predicates.ancillary_facilities_serve_lodgers: Facilities in or around the lodging are provided to meet the needs of its pilgrims or travellers.
predicates.profit_motive: The property or its facilities are operated with a purpose of making profit.
predicates.ancillary_facilities_form_part_of_choult: Facilities incidental to the lodging are treated as part of the choultry.

issues.definition: When a property-tax appeal concerns a property principally organized for pilgrims’ or travellers’ lodging, its related facilities serve those lodgers, and the operation lacks a profit motive, those facilities count as part of the choultry.

issues.legal_issue: A charitable choultry remains exempt when its incidental charges are not rent for occupation and its income, including nominal rent from an incidental facility, is used exclusively for the choultry’s charitable purpose.
material_facts: The lodging was provided without rent, although small service charges were collected for some first-floor rooms.
A small monthly rent was received from a brass cooperative store located within the campus.
The choultry’s income was insufficient to meet its maintenance expenditure, and the evidence showed that its income was used for its upkeep and charitable purpose.
The Devasthanam substantially funded the choultry’s operation.
issues.conclusion: The service charges were not rent for occupation, and the nominal rent and other income were used exclusively for the choultry; the property qualified for exemption from property tax.
issues.legal_principle: Section 83(1)(b) of the Madras District Municipalities Act, 1920 exempts choultries for which no rent is charged for occupation, as well as choultries whose occupation rent is used exclusively for charitable purposes. The Court held that nominal service charges for amenities are not necessarily rent, and that income from an incidental facility may be considered where it is used exclusively for the choultry’s charitable purpose. A person claiming an exemption must establish that the property falls within it; taxing provisions are construed strictly, and ambiguity benefits the taxpayer. The Court distinguished the cited cases concerning separate properties or premises not shown to be part of the choultry, including Sri Kanyakaparameswari Anna Satram v. Vijayawada Municipality, Kodandaram Pillai v. Municipal Council, Trichinopoly, and Pandarasannadhi v. Corporation of Madras.

rule.if: tax_exemption_appeal and property_is_choultry and (no_occupation_rent or occupation_income_used_exclusively_for_charity) and service_charges_are_not_rent

predicates.tax_exemption_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning whether property is exempt from municipal property tax as a choultry.
predicates.property_is_choultry: The property is a choultry principally intended to provide charitable lodging or shelter to pilgrims or travellers.
predicates.no_occupation_rent: No rent is charged for occupying the choultry.
predicates.occupation_income_used_exclusively_for_c: Any rent charged for occupation is used exclusively for the choultry’s charitable purpose.
predicates.service_charges_are_not_rent: Charges collected for services or amenities are not rent charged for occupying the choultry.
predicates.choultry_is_exempt_from_property_tax: The choultry qualifies for exemption from municipal property tax.

issues.definition: In a property-tax appeal, a choultry is exempt when it charges no occupation rent or uses all occupation rent exclusively for charity, and its service charges are not occupation rent.
